correctness.rationale: For m>=4, exact simplex inner products give the three absolute-Gram entries and Parseval normalization. Unsigned edge incidence Q yields Q^T Q=2I+A and QQ^T=(n-2)I+J, hence A has eigenvalues 2(n-2),n-4,-2 with stated multiplicities. Substitution gives all G eigenvalues, the positive principal gaps, and the branch change at m=7. Orthogonal splitting t=hu+z proves the global inequality, and normalizing u+epsilon z for nonprincipal top eigenvectors makes the coefficient sharp within strictly positive weights. The packaged exact-integer checker passed 262333 assertions over m=4..18, corroborating but not proving the general argument. m=3 excluded because top eigenvalue not simple.

value.rationale: The regular-simplex midpoint frame is a motivated extremal candidate studied in arXiv:2608.08695. The theorem resolves the natural sharp quantitative loss in its projection-weight objective when weights are nonuniform, valid for all real dimensions m>=4 and all nonnegative unit weights. It gives unique optimizing weights, exact complete spectrum, optimal coefficient, nontrivial eigenspace crossover, and explicit positive-weight sharpness. It does not pretend to settle the global maximal-projection problem.
